## Rule (decoded 2026-07-07, verified train ex1+ex2)

Input is **8×4** = two stacked 4×4 grids: top grid color **3**, bottom grid color **1**.
Output is **4×4**, color **2**. `out[r,c] = 2 iff top[r,c]==0 AND bottom[r,c]==0` — a **NOR**
of the two halves, recolored. Nonlinear (AND of two positions) + shape change 8×4→4×4.
Live 94-byte graph implements it as rank-1 `ConvTranspose(10→1, 2-tap dilation-4, crop→4×4)
→ Conv(1→10)` using a signed encoding so argmax picks color 2 vs 0 with no bias.

## Algorithm sketch

```
top = grid[0:4]; bot = grid[4:8]              # two 4x4 halves
out = np.where((top==0) & (bot==0), 2, 0)     # NOR, recolor to 2
```

## Cost analysis

**Live is 94, not the stale 3,503 below** (auto-diag/STATUS blocks are pre-Vamshi and
stale; `ng_current_bar.py --task 227` → manifest cost 94, sha `b12b1571…`, owner Vamshi).
`cost = memory + params` = 64 + 30. The 64 is the forced [1,1,4,4] F32 rank-1 intermediate
(16 output cells × 4 B). The 30 params = 20 source (10 in-channels × 2 vertical taps to
NOR rows i and i+4) + 10 render (1→10 one-hot output channels). **This is the forced floor**
— full proof + the one-op 200-param tradeoff in
`task227/hard_records/perfect25_and_sub94_floor.md`.

## Don't-do log

- **Perfect-25 ≤1 (zero-param Identity/Transpose/flip)** — DEAD. Rule is a nonlinear NOR
  with an 8×4→4×4 shape change; no payload-free geometric op qualifies. Both zero-param
  candidates gate 0/267 visible. Perfect-25 needs cost ≤1; min correct graph is 30 params.
- **Single-op direct ConvTranspose 10→10** — 200 params (`oneop_direct.onnx`) > 94. Deletes
  the intermediate but the fused weight is [10,10,2,1]=200. Lose.
- **Slice input to fewer color channels first** — the Slice intermediate is a full
  [1,k,30,30] canvas (≥3,600 B) that dwarfs the 64-B rank-1 plane. Lose.
- **f16 / Cast** — any Cast to a narrower dtype materialises a ≥9,000-B full-canvas
  intermediate; the 4×4 saving can't pay for it (also confirmed by 2026-05-20 spread_scan).
